body_site.evidence_quote: Bacterial DNA was extracted from stool samples

sex.notes: Gender ratio mentioned as discrepant among groups but individual participant sex not fully specified per sample

age.notes: Age correlation with bacterial abundance analyzed but individual ages not reported

control.notes: Study has control group (healthy controls, n=41) and case groups (pre-hypertension, n=56; hypertension, n=99) but individual sample assignments not provided

ancestry.notes: Participants from Chinese cohort (Kailuan community) but specific ancestry not detailed

westernized.notes: Not classified; study mentions subjects from concentrated environment with relatively small dietary differences

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not applicable; study involves unrelated human cohort and mouse models.

antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion applied uniformly to all human participants in the main cohort.

bmi.notes: Paper states no remarkable regularity of bacterial abundance based on BMI, but does not report actual BMI values.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It was composed of 41 healthy controls (SBP ≤125 mmHg, or DBP ≤80 mmHg), 56 pHTNs (125 mmHg < SBP ≤ 139 mmHg, or 80 mmHg < DBP ≤ 89 mmHg), 99 patients of HTN (140 mmHg ≤ SBP, or 90 mmHg ≤ DBP).
disease_details.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
disease_details.notes: Definitions based on Internal Guidelines for HTN classification.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples analyzed for microbial composition and function using metagenomic sequencing.

fmt_role.notes: Human donors include 2 HTN patients and 1 normotensive control; recipient mice analyzed post-transplantation.

smoker.evidence_quote: Patients suffering from cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and chronic inflammatory disease were all excluded.
smoker.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
smoker.notes: Smoking status excluded as exclusion criterion applied uniformly.

treatment.notes: Human participants explicitly excluded if on antihypertensive treatment. Drugs including statins, aspirin, insulin, metformin, nifedipine, and metoprolol not used; other drug consumption not compared due to small sample size.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve cancer staging.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve tumor staging.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Genera such as Prevotella and Klebsiella were overrepresented in individuals with pHTN or HTN. Faecalibacterium, Oscillibacter, Roseburia, Bifidobacterium, Coprococcus, and Butyrivibrio, which were enriched in healthy controls, declined in pHTN and HTN patients.
biomarker_name.section: Results — pHTN and HTN-associated genera in GM; Metabolic profiling of GM in pHTN and HTN
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified across bacterial genera and metabolites. Prevotella, Klebsiella enriched in disease; Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Bifidobacterium depleted in disease. Metabolites include phospholipids and amino acid derivatives.

biomarker_unit.notes: Relative abundance reported for bacterial biomarkers; specific units (e.g., pg/mL, nmol/L) not reported for metabolites.

biomarker_value.notes: Paper reports relative abundance changes and statistical comparisons (P values, fold-changes via OR scores) rather than absolute quantitative values for most biomarkers.

disease_response_os.notes: This is an observational/mechanistic study of hypertension pathogenesis; no overall survival data reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no survival data in paper.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not relevant to this microbiome/hypertension study; ECOG performance status not assessed.

value: reduced bacteria associated with healthy status
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Compared to the healthy controls, we found dramatically decreased microbial richness and diversity, Prevotella-dominated gut enterotype, distinct metagenomic composition with reduced bacteria associated with healthy status and overgrowth of bacteria such as Prevotella and Klebsiella.
feces_phenotype_value.section: Abstract; Results — GM diversity and enterotype; Results — Functional alteration
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes characterize dysbiosis in hypertensive and pre-hypertensive subjects compared to healthy controls.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this study focuses on hypertension, not oncology.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

value: Cohort composition: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive subjects, 99 hypertensive individuals (n=196 total)
Sequencing platform: Illumina paired-end (125-bp reads, insert size 300 bp)
Total sequencing output: 1211 Gb with average 6.18±1.43 million reads per sample
All subjects from Kailuan Group Corporation cohort, Tangshan, northern China
Hypertensive patients were newly diagnosed prior to antihypertensive treatment
Participants excluded if received antibiotics or probiotics within 8 weeks
Fecal microbiota transplantation performed in germ-free mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN)
Blood pressure measured by tail-cuff method at 10 weeks post-transplantation
HTN mice showed elevated SBP (P=0.018), DBP (P=0.019), MBP (P=0.014) vs controls
Metabolomic analysis of 124 subjects (30 controls, 31 pre-hypertensive, 63 hypertensive)
Disease classifier based on CAGs and metabolites achieved AUC=0.91 for HTN vs control
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: The cohort consisted of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pHTN, and 99 patients with primary HTN. All samples were paired-end sequenced on the Illumina platform (insert size 300 bp, read length 125 bp). At 10 weeks post-transplantation, BP of recipient mice in HTN and control group was measured by the tail-cuff method.
uncurated_metadata.section: Results — GM diversity and enterotype; Methods — Metagenomic sequencing; Methods — Animal experiments
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key experimental design and sample characteristics. Fecal microbiota transplantation is central evidence for causality.

host_species.evidence_quote: we carried out comprehensive metagenomic and metabolomic analyses in a cohort of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pre-hypertension, 99 individuals with primary hypertension, and performed fecal microbiota transplantation from patients to germ-free mice.
host_species.notes: Study includes both human subjects (Chinese individuals from Kailuan cohort) and germ-free C57BL/6L mice as recipients of human fecal microbiota.

extraction_warnings: Granularity set to sample_level per schema, but paper reports only study_level aggregates (n=41 controls, n=56 pre-hypertensive, n=99 hypertensive). No per-sample metadata provided; individual subject identifiers and sample IDs not disclosed.
control field cannot be populated per-sample without individual sample assignments to case/control groups.
sex and age reported only at group level (Table S1 mentions gender ratio discrepant among groups; age/BMI correlation analyzed but not per-sample values).

For fecal microbiota transplantation experiments, recipient mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN) are described but not as human subjects; mouse experiment is in vivo model validation, not primary human cohort sampling.
Study includes 124 subjects for metabolomic analysis (subset: 30 controls, 31 pre-hypertensive, 63 hypertensive) but individual-level metabolite and microbiota data not provided in accessible form.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'Primary hypertension (HTN)', 'HTN mice (FMT recipients)', 'Control mice (FMT recipients)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Paper does not report individual participant ages for human cohort; only age exclusion/inclusion criteria and mouse ages provided.
BMI reported as analyzed but no actual values provided for any group.
FMT donor identifiers are categorical (HTN patient 1, HTN patient 2, control) rather than study-specific IDs.
Participant-level metadata (race, ethnicity, etc.) not available in provided paper text.
Some clinical parameters (e.g., fasting blood glucose) show statistical differences between groups but actual values not consistently reported.
Study mentions gender ratio discrepancy among groups but does not provide detailed breakdown.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
biomarker_value field is empty because the paper reports relative abundance and statistical comparisons (P-values, OR scores) rather than absolute quantitative values or effect sizes for biomarkers.
biomarker_unit field is empty because units are not explicitly stated for most bacterial genera (relative abundance assumed) and metabolites.
ECOG and tumor size fields are not applicable to this hypertension microbiome mechanistic study.
disease_response_os (overall survival) is not measured in this study; it is an observational cohort study of microbiota and hypertension pathogenesis, not a survival or clinical outcome trial.
Sample-level data were not extracted because the paper reports aggregated study-level and subgroup-level statistics (means, medians, diversity indices) rather than per-participant biomarker rows.
Fecal phenotype values capture descriptive microbiota characteristics rather than quantitative measurements.
